newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit fails to capitalise on dollar's fall.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit fails to capitalise on dollar's fall.

text.p: The ringgit failed to capitalise on the fall of the dollar against the yen, trading within its recent range, dealers said.
They said an attempt to push down dollar/ringgit was met by buyers at around 2.5230, seen as a firm support level.
"You see big moves by yen but no momentum on the ringgit," said a Malaysian bank dealer.
Dollar/yen was weak in Asia on news of the first upturn in two years in Japan's trade surplus for November.
At the 1000 GMT local close, ringgit was at 2.5238/48 a dollar, up from 2.5245/55 on Tuesday.
Dealers said the ringgit also gained strength on bullish expectations that Malaysia's 1996 trade deficit will be well below the government forecast of 5.2 billion ringgit.
The Statistics Department said on Tuesday the trade shortfall in the first 10 months was only at 954.35 million.
Year-end holiday factors continued to be cited as the main reason for the ringgit's lacklustre performance.
